lesson_title: Six People, One Month, No Mistakes
hook_text: A shelter that keeps the rain out and poisons the family inside has failed. Here is the full list.
clip_script: The task: a sturdy, waterproof, easy-to-erect shelter for a family of six for a month. Sturdy: a 60 kilometre per hour wind. Waterproof: roof, walls and floor. Easy: two adults, an hour, a mallet. Six people: 21 square metres, headroom, a door. Now the part people forget. The family will cook inside with the same stove that burned their street. So: two metres between shelters, a raised stove place away from the walls, a cover that does not drip fire. A sealed tent with a stove fills with carbon monoxide, no smell, no warning. So: vents high and low, hooded against rain. A lamp hook, not candles. Then the site: a trench against runoff, water within 500 metres, toilets 50 metres away and downhill, one per twenty, a door that fastens from inside, walls you cannot see through, lit paths, nails cleared, high firm ground, room for an ambulance. Every line is a test for your model.
visual_style: Whiteboard shelter outline with labels landing: wind arrow, rain lines, floor, door; a camp plan with two-metre gaps, water point, toilets downhill; hooded vents high and low.
mood: Firm and caring, a safety briefing that matters.
pacing: Task, adjectives, fire, air, site, security, each a beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write the health and safety list for your shelter.
